objective: Proof and computation. After removing a line on the point side, the hub opens: its points are no longer tied, and the interface becomes the port patterns that the closed piece allows with that line gone, a knot-side relation of more than two patterns. Elimination through hub points then fails for some pairs, and new crossing knots appear that no chain of eliminations from one-sided knots produces. Checked on the same splices; counted and exemplified.
status: Proved by HUB-GLUE-20261102-001C-P001: after removing a line on the point side, the port patterns are exactly those the closed point piece allows without that line, a complement-closed set of not-all-equal patterns: one pair (the hub re-ties; 2-sum holds, 16 cases), two pairs (one port released, the other two tied; 716) or three (the hub becomes a knot; 388); with two or three pairs the 2-sum fails, and in the 13-point Fano splice 72 crossing knots are produced by no chain of eliminations. Two ports on the removed line stay tied, opposite under the closing line's signs (nice 4-cycles, sign-nonsingularity)
title: An opened hub creates emergence that does not compose
